DMU’s Prof. Mirza Baig Speaks at The International Conference on “Avenues and Opportunities in Pharmaceutical Research and Practice

Professor Mirza R. During the conference, he delivered an insightful and

Professor Mirza R. Baig, Program Director for the Master of Clinical Pharmacy and Professor of Pharmacy Practice at the College of Pharmacy – Dubai Medical University (DMU), was invited as a speaker at an international conference organized by Indira University, Pune, India, held on 13–14 January 2026. During the conference, he delivered an insightful and forward-looking presentation on “Simulation Safety in Pharmacy Education: Enhancing the Role of the Clinical Pharmacist in the Patient Care Process.” His talk highlighted the critical importance of simulation-based education in preparing pharmacy graduates for safe, effective, and patient-centered clinical practice.

In addition to his keynote participation at the conference, Professor Baig was also invited to speak at several prestigious pharmacy institutions in Pune, including Modern College of Pharmacy, Bharati Vidyapeeth University, and Poona College of Pharmacy. These academic interactions provided an excellent platform for knowledge exchange and academic collaboration between institutions in India and the United Arab Emirates.

During his lectures, Professor Baig showcased how Dubai Medical University stands at the forefront of innovation in health professions education by integrating advanced simulation technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and virtual reality (VR) into its pharmacy curriculum. He emphasized that DMU adopts a learner-centered, competency-based educational model, where students are trained extensively in high-fidelity simulated environments that closely replicate real clinical settings.

This progressive approach ensures that DMU pharmacy students develop strong clinical decision-making, communication, and patient safety skills before being deployed to professional experiential training sites. By allowing students to practice and refine their competencies in a controlled, risk-free environment, DMU significantly enhances patient safety while producing practice-ready clinical pharmacists.

Professor Baig’s presentations strongly reflected DMU’s commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and global best practices in pharmacy education, reinforcing the university’s reputation as a regional and international leader in simulation-based healthcare training.

Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy highlights the international academic engagement of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, who was recently invited as a panelist at the Residency Showcase & Career Strategy event organized by the Lebanese American University (LAU) School of Pharmacy. Dubai Medical University (DMU) – College of Pharmacy highlights the international academic engagement of Dr. Ahmad El Ouweini, Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice and Critical Care Clinical Pharmacist, who was recently invited as a panelist at the Residency Showcase & Career Strategy event organized by the Lebanese American University (LAU) School of Pharmacy.

The event, held at LAU, brought together PharmD students, residents, alumni, and faculty to discuss the evolving landscape of pharmacy residency training and its impact on career development. Dr. El Ouweini participated in the Alumni Panel, moderated by Dr. Mira El Masri, where he shared insights from his professional journey and highlighted the importance of advanced pharmacy training.

Drawing on his diverse experience across Lebanon and the UAE, Dr. El Ouweini reflected on his path from BPharm training in Syria, to completing his PharmD at LAU, a PGY-1 residency, and later a post-doctoral fellowship in clinical pharmacy research. Today, as a faculty member at DMU, he continues to advance clinical pharmacy education while establishing and expanding critical care services at DMU Hospital.

During the panel discussion, he emphasized how residency training shaped his clinical reasoning, teaching approach, and research capabilities. He also explained how Lebanon’s PGY-1 programs—designed in alignment with U.S. residency standards—equipped him with the competencies needed to practice confidently in international healthcare environments.
He noted that while the field has evolved from BPharm → PharmD → PGY-1, residency remains a “true investment” that enhances a pharmacist’s readiness for both local and global practice.

He encouraged students to embrace opportunities with clarity and ambition, reminding them that residency training builds not only clinical expertise but also leadership, communication, resilience, and teamwork.

Panelist in SimTalks: the Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Healthcare Simulation

As part of Simulation Week 2025 and the celebration of Simulation Champions, Dr. Sarah Sanad, Assistant Professor at the College of Nursing, participated as a panelist at the SIMTalks session, “Beyond the Bedside: The Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Simulation.” The event brought together simulation experts from the region and internationally,

As part of Simulation Week 2025 and the celebration of Simulation Champions, Dr. Sarah Sanad, Assistant Professor at the College of Nursing, participated as a panelist at the SIMTalks session, “Beyond the Bedside: The Promise and Limits of VR, AR, and AI in Simulation.” The event brought together simulation experts from the region and internationally, alongside educators, healthcare professionals, and students, to explore the evolving role of technology in clinical education.

Dr. Sanad emphasized the importance of balancing technological innovation with human-centered care, noting that empathy, intuition, and professional judgment remain essential in training future clinicians. She highlighted the need for equitable access, demonstrating that meaningful learning can be achieved through low-fidelity models, creative approaches, and collaborative partnerships, even in the absence of high-cost VR/AR/AI equipment.

Looking ahead to 2035, Dr. Sanad predicted that students will increasingly engage with AI-driven virtual environments, but she stressed that these tools must complement, not replace, real-world bedside experiences. She offered actionable recommendations for educators, including aligning technology with learning outcomes, empowering faculty to adapt tools, promoting creativity and equity, and keeping patient safety, resilience, and humanity at the core of simulation-based education.

The session highlighted both the promise and limitations of immersive technologies, reaffirming the value of blended learning models that combine virtual simulation with bedside practice to prepare competent, empathetic, and resilient healthcare professionals.

On June 12th, 2025, the College of Nursing at Dubai Medical University received a delegation from the Dubai Corporation for Ambulance Services (DCAS), led by Mr. Salem Mohammad Askar, Head of the Ambulance Training Unit, along with Mr. Sultan Nayef and Mr. Abdulrahman Kilani. The visit aimed to explore cutting-edge advancements in clinical simulation and discuss potential areas of academic and professional collaboration.

The delegation was welcomed by Prof. Basil Amarneh, Dean of the College of Nursing, and Dr. Sarah Sanad, who provided an in-depth tour of the university’s simulation and skills labs. The visitors were briefed on the organizational structure, curriculum-integrated training and assessment plans, and the advanced technologies used to deliver high-quality clinical education.

A key focus of the visit was the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into clinical education and assessment, highlighting the university’s commitment to innovation and excellence in healthcare training. Both parties also discussed promising opportunities for future collaboration, particularly in leveraging DMU’s state-of-the-art facilities for workforce development and professional training.

The College of Nursing at Dubai Medical University (DMU) proudly participated in the SANID Program, a national volunteer initiative dedicated to training individuals to effectively respond to disasters and emergencies across the UAE.

Held from June 2nd to 4th, 2025 at the DMU Building (Second Floor, Rooms 207 & 208), the program brought together nursing students and faculty members for three days of intensive training that combined lecture-based instruction with hands-on practical sessions.
The training covered a wide range of essential emergency preparedness and response skills, including:
Preparing for disasters
Leadership in crisis situations
Fire safety and prevention
Psychological reactions to disasters
Search and rescue operations
Injury triage and classification
Raising awareness about terrorism
Lifting and securing techniques
Basic first aid
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)

A highlight of the program was a comprehensive emergency simulation exercise, where participants applied all the skills learned in a realistic, scenario-based environment, enhancing their confidence and readiness to respond to public emergencies.
